XXI, 29</cite>); <cite ref="Exodus 21:29">ib.</cite> <he>בחזקת ש׳ וכ׳</he> are presumed to be safe (the owner is not bound to guard them).
<cite ref="Nedarim 37a:3">Ned. 37ᵃ</cite> <he>שכר ש׳</he> the teacher is paid for guarding the pupils (and not for the teaching itself).

<cite ref="Nedarim 37a:3">Ib.</cite> <he>גדול בר ש׳ הוא</he> does an adult need guarding? <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 5:10">Koh. R. to V, 10</cite> <he>צריך ש׳ וכ׳</he> must be watched against weasels &c.; a. fr.—Pl. <he>שִׁימּוּרִים</he>, <cite ref="U00958"><he>שִׁמּ׳</he></cite> (b. h. <cite ref="U01527"><he>שִׁמֻּרִים</he></cite>); <he>ליל ש׳</he> a night of watching.
Pes. 109ᵇ; R. Hash. 11ᵇ, a. e., v. שָׁמַר.—2) (v. שְׁמָרִים) clearing wine, straining.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 20:1:4">Y. Sabb. XX, beg. 17ᶜ</cite> <he>הותר מכלל ש׳</he> is permitted on the Holy Day as far as straining is concerned; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Beitzah 1:10:5">Y. Bets. I, 60ᵈ</cite> bot.
